output.brief:
Pellacott's 2026-built VA-220 valves are defective, and the leak-test certificates that lifted its score don't reflect real testing. The calibration contractor found the only VA-220 test rig out of service since January 2026, with no VA-220 test program on the other rigs. The 2026 certificate tables repeat four sequences that also appear in November 2025 certificates. Your own lab found 11% of unused 2026 Pellacott valves leaking at the seat. Matched claims show the same failure rate across installer groups and across firmware versions, and the Durrant-Hale valves are unaffected. Installers and firmware 4.2 are therefore not the cause. Do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates, and do not discipline installers.

Next steps: quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend its dock-to-stock status, and release stock only after Brenmoor's own helium testing. Demand rig logs from Pellacott and get a replacement supply plan from Durrant-Hale to avoid a line stoppage. Then change SupplierPath so test records need rig logs or a witnessed test, and spot-check other suppliers, since whether they have the same problem is unknown. Whether the Corlin seal or Line 3 caused the leaks is not yet separated, so don't mandate a seal change until it is.
